description:
SURFACED by the fz-go4.43 adversarial audit (at 6efa9fc16). fz-go4.43 made item_macro_call_may_define (world.rs:2747) return true for ANY non-reserved-head item-macro call, so demand_function_scope's global-module branch (world.rs:2103-2116) now includes EVERY Indexed code containing ANY such call in the homes set. publish_function_source_job (jobs/source.rs:282-300) waits on ALL of homes, and the scheduler is AND-semantics (scheduler.rs:397: !waits.iter().all(..)) — so the job only re-runs once EVERY home code is fully ScopeCode'd (macro-expanded + all definitions stashed).

CONSEQUENCE: the first still-unresolved global bare-name lookup (ANY name, not just a macro-produced one) forces ScopeCode on every file containing any opaque item-macro call, even files that cannot possibly define the wanted name. Scenario: files A..Z, ten each with one unrelated custom-macro DSL call, target fn behind its own macro in file Y — resolving one name pre-emptively scopes all 11.

BOUNDED, not a blocker: CodeState::Scoped is cached and the scan skips already-Scoped codes (world.rs:2114), so the cost is paid ONCE per program. Correctness holds (candidate-home is a pure DEMAND trigger, never feeds resolution/disambiguation — verified). Today's impact is narrow (only reserved-head-free item-macro pattern in-tree is the test DSL, fixtures2/0052x). BUT this is eager whole-surface scoping on first lookup — it works AGAINST the pull/laziness discipline (excess work is a correctness SIGNAL, not perf), and grows as item macros become common (the very feature fz-go4.43 unblocks).

TASK (holistic, not a shim): either (a) stage the homes wait — scope ONE opaque-macro candidate at a time and re-check whether the name resolved before scoping the next, so an early hit short-circuits the rest; or (b) let an item macro declare (even coarsely) the name(s)/arities it may produce, so item_macro_call_may_define can rule out unrelated calls WITHOUT expanding them. VERIFY via a --log-telemetry job trace: resolving one global name in a multi-file program with unrelated item-macro calls does NOT ScopeCode the unrelated files. Related: fz-go4.43, fz-go4.18.41 (arm-less-wait AND-semantics), the pull-discipline north star.

comments.text: LANDED at 917e002b2 (folded from wt/b6-53 4da456a19). Split the boolean code_surface_can_publish_function / item_macro_call_may_define predicates into a 3-valued FunctionSurfaceMatch enum (None<Opaque<Certain, derived Ord) via code_surface_function_match / item_macro_call_match. demand_function_scope now returns ONLY the certain fn-form home's CodeScoped wait when one exists (a plain fn/fnp/defmacro/defmodule/defprotocol/defimpl head naming the wanted name+arity, or a compiler-service form) — unrelated opaque item-macro candidates become irrelevant; otherwise STAGES opaque candidates one at a time in submission order (returns the first opaque candidate's wait; on re-run the probed code is Scoped and excluded, narrowing to the next). Net complexity DECREASE: two boolean helpers -> one classifier + a small Ord enum, no new job/fact/field. Never bundles a non-empty wait with the arm-less FunctionSourceStash (AND-semantics safe, jobs/source.rs unchanged). Termination on a truly-undefined name verified: opaque set strictly shrinks -> terminal empty return -> arm-less stash -> proper 'function X is not defined' diagnostic, no hang/spin. Order deterministic (code.ids() is a Vec, submission order). Test: drive_test.rs::compiler2_resolving_a_global_name_does_not_scope_unrelated_opaque_macro_calls — telemetry OutputCapture over Job::ScopeCode, asserts main's file IS scoped and two unrelated opaque-macro files are NEVER scoped; proven non-vacuous (reverting world.rs fails with 'got a ScopeCode(CodeId(2))'). fz-go4.43's 3 macro-DSL tests stay green. lib 1239/0/6. Adversarial audit: SOUND, all 6 risks cleared. Audit NIT (first-certain-home-wins over an untested cross-file duplicate-definition edge -> deterministic, an improvement) surfaced a latent gap: no duplicate-global-definition diagnostic -> filed fz-zbp.

title: demand_function_scope global branch eagerly scopes the WHOLE surface on the first unresolved global name (AND-semantics fan-out over every opaque item-macro call)
